provenance: Five explicitly named, sounding source voices are compiled separately; these are written voice identities, not recovered hands or aural separation. The empty oboestwo control expression is retained in engraving but is not invented as a sounding voice. EXT: Leichte Stücke, 1900; exact performance articulation remains provisional.
Read content/listen/schumann-kinderszenen-traumerei.mjs and cache/analysis/schumann-kinderszenen-traumerei.txt. Editorial sections are coarse; they are not forced alignment anchors.

Engraving only: replace the source's skip-only repeattr with the same 97-quarter span (one-quarter pickup plus 24 four-quarter bars), explicitly restoring its already-encoded repeat signs at q1 and q33. Every original pitched variable, tempo, dynamics and pedal voice remains unchanged; immutable source bytes are untouched.

The legacy published MIDI has 339 attacks versus 344 in a modern merged-staff compile, with seven differently timed grace attacks and five genuinely visible reattacks: viola C5 at q31 after its same-pitch acciaccatura; viola G4 at q42, D5 at q58 and D5 at q88.5 against sustained violatwo unisons; and bassvoicestwo A3 as the second grace before q22, tied onward. Separate unchanged source-voice extraction preserves these attacks and written ties. No exact legacy-MIDI identity is claimed.
